yarn-deadset.meaning: Every duty, condition and qualification is kept, nothing added: "A one year probation period may be required.", "We offer the chance to work from home, per Agency policy."
yarn-deadset.sense: The swaps fit: "on your CV", "new starters", "pro rata basis", "Must pass a background check", "Spotting and analysing production problems".
yarn-deadset.authenticity: Natural Australian HR English, though it barely uses slang: "Getting information across effectively and diplomatically".
yarn-deadset.register: Much lighter than level 3: a plain Australian-English localisation with almost no vernacular ("picked", "stick to", "coming up with fixes"). No swearing.
yarn-deadset.tone: Keeps the formal, informative tone of a job ad: "You must meet the following requirements by the closing date of this announcement."
yarn-deadset.flow: Reads smoothly: "To make sure you get full credit for your work experience, please put your dates of employment as month/day/year".
yarn-deadset.variety: Few vernacular terms to vary; none repeated: "picked", "stick to", "Spotting", "coming up with fixes".
yarn-deadset.essence: Unmistakably the original announcement: "This is a bargaining unit position, AFGE Council 260."

yarn-troppo.meaning: All requirements survive, but asides add judgements and claims: "the legacy systems (read: the old clunkers)", "No pressure.", "they're not fussy where", "and somebody's gotta carry them out". "so it's a union job" glosses the bargaining-unit line.
yarn-troppo.sense: Terms mostly fit ("the whole box and dice", "here's your yakka", "nutting out production problems", "Have a squiz"); "Wrangle the contents of documents" pushes "manipulate" towards forcing them.
yarn-troppo.authenticity: Natural idiom for the most part, but stock openers and tags are bolted on: "Here's one for ya.", "Yep, the whole thing.", "Not bad, ay?"
yarn-troppo.register: Heavier than level 3: a running chatty commentary on a federal job ad ("And the cherry on top", "Diplomacy, in other words."). No swearing, within vulgarity 1.
yarn-troppo.tone: A formal announcement turned jokey, with asides that undercut it: "so the lot gets published legally effective, on time and spot on. No pressure."
yarn-troppo.flow: Lively, but the tag sentences break up the requirements: "Click \"Print Preview\" to read the whole announcement before you apply. Yep, the whole thing."
yarn-troppo.variety: Leans on short tag sentences after each item: "No pressure.", "Don't skip that bit.", "Yep, the whole thing.", "Diplomacy, in other words.", "Not bad, ay?"
yarn-troppo.essence: Still the announcement, but the persona reshapes it into a pitch: "Here's one for ya. There's a job going".

yarn-dinkum.meaning: Every point is kept; "so it's a union job" is a gloss on "bargaining unit position" that hangs off the original.
yarn-dinkum.sense: Terms fit: "no worries", "spot on", "pitching in as part of a team", "Get your head around what customers need", "Have a squiz", "nutting out production problems".
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Sounds like an Australian job ad written by a person: "If you get picked at a lower grade level, no worries", "part-time work gets counted pro rata".
yarn-dinkum.register: Level 3 throughout: a steady, natural lift without turning the ad into a yarn. No swearing.
yarn-dinkum.tone: Informative and friendly, the ad's purpose intact: "You must be a U.S. Citizen or U.S. National."
yarn-dinkum.flow: Smooth throughout: "Know your way around the technical resources available for, and tied to, the Federal Register publication processes".
yarn-dinkum.variety: Varied; "ticked off" and "properly" recur but don't stand out: "all the program goals get ticked off".
yarn-dinkum.essence: Unmistakably the original announcement, retold: "This announcement might also be used to fill similar jobs in other organisations".

unharnessed.meaning: Everything kept, including the original's garble: "before they're developed for publication". Nothing added.
unharnessed.sense: Terms fit: "ticked off", "postgrad degree", "You've gotta pass a background check", "Spotting and working through production problems".
unharnessed.authenticity: Natural, but US forms are left: "on your resume", "every new hire in the U.S.", "Specialized Experience" beside "specialised".
unharnessed.register: A light level 3: plain conversational rewording with a little slang ("gotta", "ticked off", "postgrad"). No swearing.
unharnessed.tone: Formal purpose kept in a friendlier voice: "You must be a U.S. Citizen or U.S. National."
unharnessed.flow: Smooth: "Fill out a Declaration for Federal Employment, when the agency asks for it, so they can work out if you're suitable for Federal employment."
unharnessed.variety: Leans on "gotta" ("You've gotta pass", "You've gotta meet") and "Have a look" twice; little else to vary.
unharnessed.essence: Unmistakably the original announcement: "This is a bargaining unit position, AFGE Council 260."

engine.meaning: Mostly the original verbatim, but "either the punters, private sector or volunteer service" garbles the public sector into members of the public, and "paddock(s)" for academic fields muddles the education requirement.
engine.sense: Two terms take the wrong sense: "punters" for public (as in public sector), and "paddock(s)" for field(s) of study.
engine.authenticity: Stage-Australian: wrong-sense swaps dropped into unchanged federal prose, with US forms left: "Specialized Experience", "Recognizing", "on your resume".
engine.register: Essentially untranslated apart from "punters", "paddock", "new starters" and "pro rata"; far lighter than level 3.
engine.tone: Formal tone kept, but the misfired swaps jar comically in a federal ad: "in an appropriate scientific, technical, or social science paddock(s)".
engine.flow: Reads as the original, with jolts at the swaps: "The experience may have been gained in either the punters, private sector or volunteer service."
engine.variety: Only a couple of swaps, one of them repeated: "paddock(s)" twice.
engine.essence: Recognisably the original since it is mostly the original: "We offer opportunities for telework, per Agency policy."

yarn-deadset.quote: Understand and properly look after customers' needs across every part of the Federal Register publication process
yarn-deadset.original: Understand and appropriately address customer needs associated with all aspects of the Federal Register publication process
yarn-deadset.why: Accurate, but the text stays near-formal throughout; under the brief's weight.

yarn-troppo.quote: Here's one for ya. There's a job going, and here's what it involves at the GS-12.
yarn-troppo.original: The following are the duties of this position at the GS-12.
yarn-troppo.why: Stock opener; recasts the announcement as a pitch.

yarn-troppo.quote: the legacy systems (read: the old clunkers)
yarn-troppo.why: Adds a judgement the original doesn't make.
One of many tag sentences; flippant about legal accuracy, and a tic across the text.

yarn-troppo.quote: and somebody's gotta carry them out
yarn-troppo.original: in fulfillment of the Office of the Federal Register's program responsibilities
yarn-troppo.why: Adds an editorial aside to a duty.

yarn-dinkum.original: This is a bargaining unit position, AFGE Council 260.
yarn-dinkum.why: A fair gloss, though slightly simplifies what a bargaining unit position means.

unharnessed.quote: put down how many hours a week you worked on your resume
unharnessed.original: indicate number of hours worked per week on your resume
unharnessed.why: US "resume" left where Australians say CV or résumé.

unharnessed.quote: Specialized Experience: For the GS-09, you need one year of specialised experience
unharnessed.original: Specialized Experience: For the GS-09, you must have one year of specialized experience
unharnessed.why: Mixed US and Australian spelling in the same line.

unharnessed.quote: every new hire in the U.S.
unharnessed.original: all new hires in the U.S.
unharnessed.why: US "new hire" left; "new starter" is local.

engine.quote: The experience may have been gained in either the punters, private sector or volunteer service.
engine.original: The experience may have been gained in either the public, private sector or volunteer service.
engine.why: "punters" means customers or gamblers; the public sector becomes nonsense.

engine.quote: in an appropriate scientific, technical, or social science paddock(s)
engine.original: in an appropriate scientific, technical, or social science field(s)
engine.why: "paddock" is a farm field, not a field of study; the requirement becomes garbled.

engine.quote: Specialized Experience: For the GS-09, you must have one year of specialised experience
engine.original: Specialized Experience: For the GS-09, you must have one year of specialized experience
engine.why: Mixed spellings in one line; US forms left elsewhere.

summaries.yarn-deadset: Accurate, clean Australian localisation, but well under level 3.
summaries.yarn-troppo: Idiomatic and lively but over-embellished for level 3, with a flippant tag-sentence tic.
summaries.yarn-dinkum: Natural, faithful and pitched exactly at level 3; the best of the set.
summaries.unharnessed: Faithful and readable, lightly Aussie, with some US forms left.
summaries.engine: Essentially untranslated, with two wrong-sense swaps that garble the requirements.
